acts.title: Indian Evidence Act, 1872
acts.description: An Act to consolidate, define and amend the law of Evidence in India.

sections.title: Interpretation-clause
sections.content: In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context: "Court", "Fact", "Relevant", "Facts in issue", "Document", "Evidence", "Proved", "Disproved", "Not proved", "India".

sections.title: Admissibility of electronic records
sections.content: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be also a document...

sections.title: Burden of proof
sections.content: Whoever desires any Court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist.

sections.title: Court may presume existence of certain facts
sections.content: The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business.

acts.title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
acts.description: An Act to consolidate and amend the provisions relating to offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

sections.title: Murder
sections.content: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.title: Organised crime
sections.content: Any continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, cyber-crimes having severe consequences, committed by any person as a member of an organised crime syndicate.

acts.title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
acts.description: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Criminal Procedure.

sections.title: Arrest without Warrant
sections.content: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits, in the presence of a police officer, a cognizable offence.

sections.title: Information in cognizable cases
sections.content: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing.

notes.title: Section 65B – Electronic Records (Notes)
notes.content:
Important factors for 65B certificate:
1. The device must be in regular lawful use during the period.
2. The information was fed into the computer in ordinary course.
3. The computer was operating properly.
4. Arjun Panditrao Khotkar holds that oral evidence cannot substitute a written certificate.

notes.title: Amendment to Evidence Act, 1872 (2023)
notes.content: Key amendments summarized: Harmonization with modern cloud storage, cryptographic hash integrity checks, and certified hash generators.

notes.title: Digital Evidence – Key Points
notes.content: Maintain strict hash-matching reports from seizure to court presentation. Any mismatch in MD5 or SHA-256 makes it inadmissible.

notes.title: Chain of Custody – Case Pointers
notes.content: Landmark rulings on seizure memo timestamps and independent witnesses for hardware cloning in cyber forensics.

notes.title: Relevant Notifications – Evidence Act
notes.content: List of authorized state and central cyber examiners under Section 79A of IT Act read with Evidence provisions.

faqs.question: How do I search for a specific Act or Rule?
faqs.answer: Use the top universal search bar on the Dashboard or browse the dedicated Acts and Rules pages. You can search by Act title, year, section number, or keywords. For more advanced criteria, click the "Advanced Search" button.

faqs.question: How can I access the latest Amendments?
faqs.answer: Navigate to the "Amendments & Updates" section from the sidebar. Here, all legal amendments, government notifications, corrigenda, and newly inserted sections are updated in real time with gazette citations.

faqs.question: Can I save my notes and bookmarks?
faqs.answer: Yes! While viewing any Act, Rule, or Section, click the bookmark icon to save it to your Bookmarks dashboard. You can also write structured personal legal notes, attach tags, import PDF notes, and export notes as PDF.

faqs.question: How do I manage my subscription?
faqs.answer: Visit the "Subscription Details" page from the sidebar. You can review your active plan, valid until date, remaining days, download GST tax invoices, update billing details, renew your plan, or manage your package tier.
